title: Agentic coding is now multiplayer: Introducing Slack Code
source_used: Adaderana Biz English (carries Slack’s own announcement text)
key_facts: Slack has introduced Slack Code, a way for teams to work with AI coding agents inside Slack.
It creates dedicated code channels for specific coding sessions or projects.
Teams can follow conversations, plans, code differences and live previews through dedicated tabs.
Teams can tag coding agents including Claude Code, Devin, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT and Vercel agents to start tasks.
Developers, product managers, designers and non-technical teammates share the same workspace.
It uses Slack’s existing security model, permissions and admin controls; humans stay involved in important decisions.
It is available across Slack plans.
quote_evidence: Slack Code creates dedicated code channels for specific coding sessions or projects, keeping development work focused and organised.
Built with Slack’s existing security model, permissions, and admin controls, agents operate securely while humans remain involved in important decisions.
why_it_matters_hint: Brings AI-assisted coding into a shared team space rather than one developer’s private session.
event_date: Announced on or before 5 Oct 2026 (exact date not stated)
notes: Text reads as Slack’s own announcement carried by Adaderana Biz English; claims about security and speed are the company’s.
